List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS

IIT students leaving India
*81. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that twenty per
cent of the IITians are still leaving India
inspite of globalisation and liberalisation;
(b) whether Government have any
statistics indicating the number of IITians
who have left India during the last three
years, year-wise and institution-wise; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government to stop this brain-drain?
Statutory Authority for private TV
channels
*82. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of  INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are considering
a separate statutory authority for regulating
the functioning of private television channels
in the wake of spurt in their number;
(b) whether TRAI has decided to come
out with separate national  policies on
broadcasting and distribution of television
channels and FM radio;
(c) if so, whether Government have
taken the view of the media experts and
others in this regard; and
(d) if so, whether any concrete proposal
in this regard has been worked out?
NCERT text books in CBSE affiliated
schools
*83. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that NCERT
published text books are studied exclusively
by students in the CBSE affiliated schools;
(b) the subjects in which NCERT books
are exclusively prescribed and since when;
(c) number of times revisions, if any,
carried out in the originally published books
on the respective subjects;

followed in carrying out such revisions on
each occasion;
(e) whether NCERT book (s) on any
subject are presently undergoing revision;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) the reasons therefor?
Revival of tea plantations in
Himachal Pradesh
†*84. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Tea Board is taking
steps to revive the old tea plantations in
Himachal Pradesh;
(b) the area of land covered under the
old tea plantations in the State;
(c) whether the Tea Board is considering
to give a package to the State to save the
Kangra tea industry; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Foreign investment in education
†*85. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
any decision to allow the foreign capital
investment in the field of education;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard and the
areas in the field of education decided to be
given priority for the purpose; and
(c) the percentage of foreign capital
investment which has been decided to be
allowed in each field of education?
Schemes for tribals in Kerala
*86. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the media reports about the misery of tribals
in Kerala;
(b) if so, the action taken in this regard;
(c) whether any study or steps have
been initiated to prevent depletion of the
bio-diversity in the region; and
(d) if so, whether any schemes have been
initiated to provide land and work for the
jobless tribals of Wayanad district of
Kerala?
Special grant to colleges
*87. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the University Grants
Commission has chalked out a scheme to
give special grant to the colleges showing
good performance to enable them to achieve
higher standards;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether such colleges have since
been identified; and
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise?
Opening of farm trade
*88. SHRI MANOJ BHATTA-
CHARYA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the trade representatives
from different countries recently met at

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the July 12, 2004/Asadha 21, 1926 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Culture; Development of North-
Eastern Region; Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Human Resource
Development; Information and Broadcasting; Law and Justice; Parliamentary
Affairs; Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Urban Development;
Urban Employment and Poverty Alleviation)
Total number of questions—73
Subsidy to fishing vessels
161. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether MPEDA has a scheme to
extend diesel oil subsidy to fishing vessels
engaged in export of marine products;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) how much money has been released
by MPEDA in 2003-04 under this scheme;
(d) the estimates for 2004-05; and
(e) the steps taken to assist the fishing
vessel owners?
Subsidies for export of grains
162. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the facilities and subsidies provided
to private traders to export grains;
(b) whether traders are demanding more
subsidies; and
(c) if so, Government's reaction
thereto?
Support price for tobacco
163. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether tobacco farmers of Andhra
Pradesh have sought support price in view
of low prices of tobacco in the market; and
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto?
Agreement in WTO
164. SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether in a bid to reach an
agreement on a negotiating framework for
key issues like agriculture and non-
agriculture, the World Trade Organisation
General Council Chairman has urged
members to work towards arriving at a
shared understanding of the package as
early as possible;
(b) if so, whether Government have
made any efforts with other countries to
solve agriculture norms/non-agriculture
issues in the WTO; and

and by when a final decision is likely to be

Revival of tea sector in West Bengal
165. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any proposal from the Government of West
Bengal for reviving the ailing tea sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the steps Government
have taken thereon?
Tea auctions
166. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
restrict the sale of tea through auctions;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the measures taken to bring the tea
produced by the small and marginal growers
to the auctions?
Closure of tea gardens
167. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number
of tea gardens have been closed/abandoned
in various parts of the country during the
last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the number of workers rendered
unemployed due to the closure;
(d) whether Government have provided
any relief package to the affected workers;
(e) whether Government propose any
comprehensive Plan to service the
plantation sector; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Industrial package for Himachal
Pradesh
†168. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the concessions to be given for
setting up industries in Himachal Pradesh
under the industrial package given by
Government;
(b) whether the proposals for setting
up of Industries have been invited by the
State Government from the industries
which are to be benefited under this scheme;
(c) the number of proposals received
by the State Government for setting up of
new industries under this scheme after
getting the above package; and
(d) if so, the details of the steps taken
by the State Government?
Foodgrains exports
169. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that foodgrain
exports may decline below ten lakh tonnes
this fiscal year;
(b) whether it is a fact that no new
contracts are being signed as Government
have not declared an export policy; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to accelerate formulation of the
export policy?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

been exported during the last three years
